Question Bank Management: The default list call, with the type parameter omitted, returns questions of every status rather than only "quiz-type" ones as the default's name misleadingly implies.
column3:
1. Log in as a trainer who has authored questions in ≥2 different statuses.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/trainer/question-bank with no type query parameter.
3. Inspect the returned list's status values.
4. Confirm questions of every status are present, not just one.
column4: 1. 200 OK; questions of ALL statuses are returned — the default "type=QUIZ" behaves identically to "type=ALL", not as a status filter.
column5: - Caller has authored questions in ≥2 different statuses.

Question Bank Management: The question list is always scoped to the caller's own authored questions — one trainer never sees another trainer's bank entries here.
column3:
1. Log in as Trainer A and prepare/send GET /api/v1/trainer/question-bank; note the returned questions.
2. Log out and log in as Trainer B; repeat the same call.
3. Compare both result sets.
4. Confirm neither list contains the other trainer's questions.
column4: 1. Each call returns only that trainer's own questions — no cross-trainer leakage in this list endpoint (correctIndex is also never included in this list DTO, unlike SectionQuestionController's lists).
column5: - Both trainers have authored ≥1 question each.

Question Bank Management: COURSE_MANAGER does NOT actually have access to the whole question-bank surface, despite holding CREATE_AND_MANAGE_EXAMS_CM — that authority is absent from this endpoint's @PreAuthorize, so COURSE_MANAGER is rejected with 403 exactly like a plain LEARNER; only TRAINER, ADMINISTRATOR, or a caller with MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES can reach it (RolePermissionDataInitializer seeds COURSE_MANAGER with only {VIEW_PLATFORM_DASHBOARD, CREATE_AND_MANAGE_EXAMS_CM} — neither satisfies MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK/MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES/ADMINISTRATOR).
column3:
1. Log in as a COURSE_MANAGER (holding only CREATE_AND_MANAGE_EXAMS_CM per the seeded role) and prepare/send GET /api/v1/trainer/question-bank; inspect the response.
2. Log out and log in as a plain LEARNER; repeat the same call.
3. Log out and log in as a TRAINER (holds MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK); repeat the same call.
4. Compare all three response statuses.
column4:
1. Step 1: 403 Forbidden — CREATE_AND_MANAGE_EXAMS_CM is not one of the authorities/roles this endpoint checks.
2. Step 2: 403 Forbidden, same outcome as COURSE_MANAGER.
3. Step 3-4: 200 OK for the TRAINER, who holds MANAGE_QUESTION_BANK.
column5: - COURSE_MANAGER, LEARNER, and TRAINER accounts available.

Question Bank Management: Creating a standalone (non-group) question correctly persists the supplied categoryId (regression check: createQuestionBankGroup previously hardcoded category=null on create for single questions; now resolves QuestionCategory by id, matching updateQuestionBankGroup's existing !isGroup lookup).
column3:
1. Log in as an eligible role and confirm a valid categoryId (e.g. 5) exists.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/trainer/question-bank body {"categoryId":5,"subQuestions":[{"questionText":"Q1",...}]} (isGroup=false shape, single question, no passageText).
3. Send the request and note the created id.
4. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/trainer/question-bank/detail/{id}?isGroup=false; inspect the categoryId field.
column4: 1. Step 4: the returned categoryId is 5, matching what was supplied — create and update now behave identically for this field.
column5: - Logged in as an eligible role; a valid categoryId=5 exists.

column3:

2. Send the request and note the created groupId.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/trainer/question-bank/detail/{groupId}?isGroup=true; inspect the returned categoryId and confirm via the sub-question rows that no QuestionCategory was set.
column4: 1. Step 3: the returned categoryId reflects the group's groupTypeParam (derived from skillParamId), NOT QuestionCategory id 5; every sub-question persists with QuestionCategory=null — categoryId always means group-type when passageText is non-blank, on both create and update.

column3:

2. Log out and log in as Trainer B.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/trainer/question-bank/detail/{thatGroupId}?isGroup=true.
4. Inspect the response status and body.
column4: 1. Step 3-4: 200 OK — Trainer B successfully retrieves Trainer A's empty group's passage/metadata, bypassing the ownership check that would otherwise apply to a non-empty group.
column5: - An empty (zero sub-question) group exists, owned by Trainer A.

Question Bank Management: Editing a single question is a full delete+recreate, so the question's database id changes after every edit.
column3:
1. Log in as the question's owner and note its current id.
2. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/trainer/question-bank/{id}?isGroup=false with updated text.
3. Re-fetch the question via the list endpoint.
4. Compare the id shown now against the id noted in step 1.
column4: 1. Step 3-4: the question now has a DIFFERENT id than before the edit — any external reference to the old id (e.g. a lesson_quizzes link) would now point at a deleted row.
column5: - An owned single question exists, referenced from elsewhere (e.g. attached to a lesson quiz) if possible to also observe the broken reference.

Question Bank Management: The same empty-group ownership-check bypass allows a caller to overwrite/repopulate another trainer's empty group with new content — more serious than the read-only bypass, since this is a write.
column3:
1. As Trainer A, have an empty group (per QUESTIONBANK_FT08) and note its id.
2. Log out and log in as Trainer B.
3. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/trainer/question-bank/{emptyGroupOwnedByA}?isGroup=true with a new passage and new subQuestions.
4. Inspect the response and confirm the group's id is unchanged but now holds Trainer B's content.
column4: 1. 200 OK — Trainer B's new sub-questions are saved into Trainer A's group id, with the group's own id unchanged; any external reference to that group id now serves Trainer B's content under Trainer A's original group identity.
column5: - An empty group owned by Trainer A exists; caller is Trainer B.
